title: What makes a RPG Maker game look like "RPG Maker "?

posts.author: Blackfield
posts.body:
Hi all,
You often hear people say "that already looks like a RPG Maker game, pass for me". So, just out of fun, let's discuss what makes an RPG Maker game look like "RPG Maker". I'll start:
The textboxes
The chubby characters
The RTP assets
The grid graphics
The battle system in general
The menu
Anything else comes to mind? - and yes, I'm planning on trying to eliminate as many of these points as possible. Ideas for that:
the textboxes - busts!!, textbox graphic, name field
chubby characters - sprite height modifier for MZ
RTP assets/Grid graphics - parallax mapping
the battle system - several plugins to make it feel more alive
The menu - several plugins

posts.author: Kanok
posts.body: Honestly, for most, it's the RTP assets being heavily used. There are lots of DLC people could use, but choose not to or if they attach art to a project, they don't bother to use anything outside of the RTP for other assets. Basically, a project showing no actual work being put into it. The RTP, when you get down to it, is for prototyping. One must actually put in the work of adding in customized systems with plugins, new art assets and music, etc. When I see the RTP being used, even with "cutscene" artwork or message busts, I immediately don't even give it a second thought. And sadly, a good majority are like that. From the 2000/2003 days when it wasn't even officially released up to MZ, a lot of projects just stick with the RTP to get a project out quick.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
If we're talking specifically "looks" it's usually the use of RTP graphics and scene layouts (including menus, battle scene, etc).
Also almost every RPG Maker game is top down with grid based movement and controls.

posts.author: Skurge
posts.body:
RTP graphics are that recognizable across a broad range of games it's become basically a staple for RPG Maker, it's sort of like bean mouth or "calArts" with cartoons these days, you immediately recognize it.
As for everything else, typically grid movement- identical UI, the music especially and the sound effects have been recycled over many iterations of RPG maker it's again recognizable.
Not to say the RTP assets are terrible- there are some good ones there but it's depressing that the art direction hasn't changed much since XP with characters having giant heads and minuscule bodies almost being chubi, the more cuter the graphics are the less I can take a game seriously even if they try to be one of those horror themed ones.
You almost have to replace the visuals and sound entirely and maybe even change up the mechanics as a whole to avoid that "RPG Maker game" feel but it's a very difficult task. I don't play a great variety of games anymore due to trying to work on my own project- but if I come across a game and it's been done with RPG maker it's pretty hard to disguise it from me so I suppose it's really dependent on how experienced you are with it.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
I'm going to split hairs a little.
1.  What makes it look (physically) like an RPG Maker Game?
The default assets.  Obvious answer.
2.  What makes it look (low effort, barely worked on, no love thrown in) like an RPG Maker Game?
Anything that screams "shovelware".
Poor spelling.
Bad grammar.
Basic combat (exploit elemental weaknesses, no gimmicks).
Simplistic themes.
Simplistic characters.
Text written by 6th grader.
Assets used poorly (even default RTP ones).
Bad mapping (overcluttered or almost nothing in the map, among other issues).
Bland stories (Mystery Box, In Media Res Openings, and Anime Tropes are among the most used and cringe these days).
Bland combat (if there are mechanics, the mechanics are boring as crap.  Stagger bars?  Weird gimmicks about "not making things dead", and instead "being a convoluted mess in hopes it will feel deeper than it is").
Poor color choices (in those who utilize their own assets, it becomes clear who has taken art classes, as you can see immediately who knows anything about color theory and readability).
Bad combat animations (low effort, very quick, or very overly long).
Put simply, I've seen plenty of AAA games that "make it look like an RPG Maker game".

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
As others have said, I think the thing that generally makes a game
look like RPGMaker
is just the default assets that come with the engine. Of course, those default assets include the default window skin, which means the appearance of the menus is absolutely part of it.
I don't think the battle system is actually a factor here – that style of battle system predates RPGMaker, after all.
I don't think grid-based graphics have anything to do with what makes a game look like RPGMaker either. Plenty of non-RPGMaker games use grid-based graphics.
Kanok said:
The RTP, when you get down to it, is for prototyping.
Click to expand...
What? No, an asset set like the RTP is not something that should be thought of as "for prototyping". If you want something just for prototyping, use
this
. You can certainly use RTP for prototyping if you want, but it's totally wrong to claim that that's its purpose.
But I do agree that, if you're using RTP, you really should go to some lengths to augment and expand it a little based on the demands of your game.
Indinera said:
Using the RTP music and the sounds
Click to expand...
Music sure, but… I don't think you can count the sounds as part of what makes a game sound like RPGMaker (unless it's specifically that they didn't change the
default
sounds set in the database). I believe the RTP sound library doesn't even originate from RPGMaker itself – several of the sounds are very similar to sounds I've heard in completely unrelated games, so I strongly suspect they just found a generic game sound library somewhere and licensed it for their engine.
Even if I were to decide to make a game with no RTP, I would probably keep the following:
The sound library. Of course, I'd change all the default sounds in the database. Might also add some custom sounds.
The animation frames. I'd probably delete the default animations from the database though and make my own from scratch. They'd use the same frames, sure, but in different ways.
Maaaybe some of the terrain graphics. Making an entirely new set of terrain graphics is a huge task. Though, it's possible I'd instead grab one of the popular dlc tilesets, depending on what fits the game.
In other words, I would
never
make a game that utterly avoids the RTP completely. It might
mostly
avoid RTP, but not entirely.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
You can't escape it, if you're making a long game with limited budget or aren't an artist yourself. There's maybe 1 set of DLC tilesets that has enough variation for full game (and they're already used in many games). Same thing with (at least animated) enemies, everybody uses the same ones. And all the animated battlers are made with 3 frame motions (standard for rpg maker), which reveals the rpg maker like visuals. (EDIT: ok there's dragonbones, but they're the same battlers everyone uses)
But yeah, a lot of stuff has already been said. In addition to the big stuff, replace/modify the small elements also, use pixel movement, no chibi style, add some moving elements to the maps, use character sprite animations, change the default scene transitions, make menu/battle ui not follow the standard layout (or plugin typical layout), change battler positions, add more frames to battler animations (if you have the money), use action sequences that make sense, add battle camera with dynamic elements (if that fits your style).

posts.author: ElvenNeko

So do not focus on it, just make a good game and nobody will care what engine it is uisng.

GE. the RPG Maker XL game I'm tidying up just now:

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
Blackfield said:
The textboxes
The chubby characters
The RTP assets
The grid graphics
The battle system in general
The menu
Click to expand...
Well on my last RPG Maker game,
I don't use the default text box layout.
I don't use 'chubby' characters.
I don't use any default assets.
The standard grid system is not obvious.
There is no battle system, hits are handled on the normal screen and depreciate a heart shaped life meter.
I have changed all the in game menus and added additional screens.
I have added a bespoke hud.
I have added bespoke graphic object based animations.
I have added bespoke dynamic lighting objects (as part of the gameplay mechanic).
I have changed all the bespoke music and sounds.
I have changes the save game screens to include non-standard data in the save file.
I'm not saying it is a good game but I don't think it stands out as a too obvious RPG Maker game to the average person.

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
If the movement is limited to left and right to enter different areas 'rooms' or through on screen objects, doors climbing up and down staircases or ladders, it changes the general 'feel' of the game to me. People expect RPG Maker games to be a top-down map view, but basically you have a grid you can map however you want.
Also isometric views are possible to do, and easier if you have a version with multi level map tiling.
